facts.claim: Anthropic’s tool search docs (checked November 2026): Claude’s ability to pick the right tool degrades once more than 30–50 tools are available.
Anthropic’s tool search docs: a typical setup of five servers (GitHub, Slack, Sentry, Grafana, Splunk) can use about 55,000 tokens on tool definitions before any work starts.
Anthropic’s tool search docs (vendor-reported): searching for tools typically cuts the tokens spent on definitions by over 85%, loading only the 3–5 tools a request needs.
Anthropic’s engineering post (November 24, 2025, vendor-reported): on its tool-use tests, Claude Opus 4 picked right 49% of the time with every tool loaded and 74% with tool search.
Anthropic’s tool search docs: each search returns up to 5 matching tools by default, and a request may hold up to 10,000 tools waiting to be found.
The MCP specification (version 2026-07-28): a server’s list of tools may change over time, and a server that says so should notify clients when it does.
Invariant Labs (April 1, 2025) call it a rug pull: a malicious server can change a tool’s description after the client has already approved it.
Invariant Labs (April 1, 2025) advise clients to pin each server and its tools, checking every tool description against a stored fingerprint before it runs.
Invariant Labs (April 1, 2025) showed a tool whose description hid an order to read the user’s SSH key file and send it along: the person never saw it, the model did.
The MCP specification (version 2026-07-28): clients must treat what a tool says about itself as untrusted unless it comes from a trusted server.
The MCP specification (version 2026-07-28): clients should show a tool’s inputs to the person before calling the server, so data can’t leak out by accident or on purpose.
The MCP specification (version 2026-07-28): a server reached over the web signs people in with OAuth 2.1, so the assistant acts for that person with a pass the server’s own sign-in issued.
The MCP specification (version 2026-07-28): a server must check that a pass was issued for it, and must not accept or pass on any other.
The MCP specification (version 2026-07-28): a server run on the same computer, over standard input and output, takes its keys from its environment instead of this sign-in.
